messages:
Nina (Customer Success): Hey team — ACME reported their demo tenant showed 0 credits ~00:03 local time, but their billing page says refill at 00:00. API was returning 429 for a few requests. Can someone explain timing?
Ben (SRE): Which timezone is the tenant set to and do we have tenant id?
Nina (Customer Success): Tenant: acme-demo-23, timezone reported by customer: America/Los_Angeles (PST). They said UI still showed remaining credits until midnight PST, then went to 0 a few minutes after.
Maya (Support): Quick note: our official reset boundary is 00:00 UTC by default for monthly buckets unless org has proration/plan migration. UI displays local tz conversions and may be cached. Could be a cache/invalidation lag.
Liam (Billing): For reserved accounts we do monthly recalcs at 00:00 UTC and write new bucket state to billing DB, then invalidate caches. If the DB write was on time but cache purge delayed, UI could show stale values while API (authoritative) returns 429 because token checks hit cache/ratelimiter layer.
Ben (SRE): Can we get logs for tenant acme-demo-23 around 1777770000? Also want the API 429 responses — headers (x-rl-reset etc) if available.
Nina (Customer Success): Pasted headers customer captured: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1777770055
x-request-id: abc-123
```
Ben (SRE): Good, reset header points to 1777770055 (55s after root). That looks like the token bucket reset wallclock in UTC ms? We store the reset as epoch seconds. If their client clocks are local, they might see mismatch.
Maya (Support): Repro suggestion for support teams: ask customer to call the usage endpoint right after they see UI discrepancy: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/acme-demo-23/credits
```
Response contains fields: remaining_tokens, refill_at (epoch). If refill_at <= now and remaining_tokens==0 then API is authoritative.
Ben (SRE): I checked infra: billing job ran at 1777770000 UTC and wrote new balance. Cache invalidation job (redis key purge) had a slight queue delay due to a burst of canary telemetry; purge finished at 1777770038. That explains the UI showing old value until purge then briefly showing zero while clients retried.
ops-bot: billing-job acme-demo-23 completed (id: job-9845) at 1777770000; cache-purge finished at 1777770038; rate-limiter counters reset at 1777770055.
Liam (Billing): TL;DR: reset boundary = 00:00 UTC. Visible UI timezones are converted client-side, and intermediate cache windows can show stale values for a couple minutes. We should explain to customer.
Nina (Customer Success): Thanks. Customer also noticed long-running websocket session still allowed a few streaming responses after midnight, then closed. Any notes?
Ben (SRE): Websocket connections have a local in-memory allowance to avoid interrupting streams mid-request — we allow in-flight tokens for up to 30s after refill boundary to finish. After that we enforce new quota. That would explain a short tail.
Maya (Support): Proposed reply for customer: keep it short — explain reset happens at 00:00 UTC, UI converts to their timezone and may show cached values up to ~2 minutes after reset. Streaming sessions may finish inflight (~30s). Ask for any request IDs if they still see 429 after 5 minutes from their local 00:00. :thumbsup:
Nina (Customer Success): I'll send that. Any ops action?
Ben (SRE): Action: increase cache purge priority for billing keys during monthly run and add metric to alert if purge > 60s. Filed INF-4523.
ops-bot: INF-4523 created by ben — Increase billing cache purge priority; monitor purge latency.
Maya (Support): Marking thread resolved from support side. If customer responds with continued issues, escalate back. :white_check_mark:
